title: Prehospital Incidence of Obstetric and Gynecologic Emergencies - A Retrospective Cohort Analysis
summary:
Current data on the absolute frequency of prehospital births and prehospital obstetric or gynecologic emergencies are lacking for the Federal Republic of Germany.
Obstetric and gynecologic emergencies are rare in absolute terms. Emergency physicians are not routinized in the management of these specific conditions. It is unclear whether uncertainty and lack of routine also result in a lack of quality care for these conditions. This is one of the aims of this study.
conditions: Pain and other conditions associated with female genital organs and menstrual cycle

interventions.name:
The data analysis is based on all emergency medical interventions with a suspected gynecological and/or obstetric diagnosis documented by the Department of Emergency Medicine at Ulm University Hospital in the period from January 1, 2015 to September 31, 2023.
According to the primary and secondary

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
All emergency medical interventions with a suspected gynecological or obstetric diagnosis 

Suspected gynecological diagnosis documented in the EPRO-5.1-ABCDE (MIND 3.1) Operational Protocol (ITEM 4. Gynecologic/obstetric diagnosis: pregnancy > 35 weeks gestation, delivery, ectopic pregnancy, eclampsia, vaginal bleeding, other).

Patients with a diagnosis of "acute abdomen" are included for differential diagnosis and manually assessed.

Patients aged 12 to 45 years with a suspected diagnosis of "pulmonary embolism" or "hypertensive derailment/hypertensive emergency" are primarily included and manually evaluated as a possible concomitant disease of pregnancy (increased risk of thromboembolism, pregnancy-associated hypertension - eclampsia).
Exclusion criteria:
All non-gynecological/obstetric diagnoses except "acute abdomen", "pulmonary embolism", "hypertension".
